quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Hi team, a quick reminder that timesheets for the last two weeks are still missing from about a third of you. Payroll closes on Thursday at noon, and anything submitted after that will be paid in the next cycle, which means waiting another month. Please complete yours today, even if you are unsure about a few hours; you can always correct them later. Thanks, Naomi
quests.question: Why did Naomi write this email?
options: To announce a change in pay dates
To explain how payroll works
To urge staff to submit their timesheets
To ask staff to check their pay slips
quests.correctAnswer: To urge staff to submit their timesheets
quests.hint: Think about what Naomi wants people to do after reading, not just what she describes.
quests.explanation: The reminder, the deadline and the request to "complete yours today" all push staff to act. Payroll details appear only as the reason the deadline matters.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Dear parents, because of a burst pipe in the sports hall, the school will close at noon on Wednesday. Buses will run at 12:15 as usual, but children whose parents cannot collect them early may stay in the library until the normal finishing time. Please let the office know by Tuesday evening if your child will stay. We apologise for the disruption.
quests.question: What are parents asked to do by Tuesday evening?
options: Arrange a repair of the sports hall pipe
Tell the office if their child will stay at school
Collect their children at noon from the school gates
Send a note about the bus times to the office
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the office if their child will stay at school
quests.hint: A deadline in a school message is tied to one specific request.
quests.explanation: The only action linked to Tuesday evening is informing the office. Collecting children at noon is a separate, later event.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Our mobile app will be unavailable on Saturday between 1:00 and 5:00 a.m. while we install security improvements. During this time you will not be able to log in, check balances or make payments. Card payments, cash machines and telephone banking will work normally. We recommend completing any urgent transfers before midnight on Friday.
quests.question: Why has the bank published this notice about its app?
options: To introduce new card payments from Saturday
To announce a new mobile app for all customers
To ask customers to visit a branch in person
To warn customers about a temporary service interruption
quests.correctAnswer: To warn customers about a temporary service interruption
quests.hint: Most of the notice describes what will and will not work. What does that add up to?
quests.explanation: The notice tells customers when the app will be down and what still works, so its purpose is a warning. It says nothing about a new app or new card features.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear Mr. Amsel, we look forward to welcoming you to the Lakeside Inn on 12 August. Because of building work near the main entrance, we recommend using the side gate on Pine Road, where a porter will be waiting to help with luggage. If you expect to arrive after 9 p.m., please call us so we can keep your room key at reception. Warm regards, The Lakeside Inn team
quests.question: Why should Mr. Amsel call the hotel?
options: To book a porter for the morning
To arrange a late arrival
To ask about the building work
To change the date of his stay
quests.correctAnswer: To arrange a late arrival
quests.hint: The request in the message depends on a condition about time.
quests.explanation: The call is needed only if he arrives after 9 p.m., so the reason is to arrange a late arrival. The porter and the side gate are offered without any call.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Important: your flight to Lisbon on 3 May now departs at 14:40 instead of 11:15. The change is due to a scheduling adjustment and does not affect your baggage allowance. If the new time does not suit you, you may choose a different flight or ask for a full refund within fourteen days of receiving this message. No action is needed if you are happy with the new time.
quests.question: What must a passenger do if the new time is acceptable?
options: Choose a different flight
Confirm by phone
Nothing further
Request a refund
quests.correctAnswer: Nothing further
quests.hint: The last sentence tells you whether the passenger has any task.
quests.explanation: "No action is needed" means nothing further must be done. The phone call, refund and other flights are options only for people who dislike the new time.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Welcome to Old Town Walking Tours! Our guides lead free two-hour walks every morning at ten from the fountain on Market Square. Tours are given in English, and no booking is needed, though groups of more than eight are asked to email ahead. Guides work for tips only, so many visitors choose to give a few coins at the end if they enjoyed the tour.
quests.question: How do the guides earn their money?
options: From a ticket sold at the fountain
From voluntary payments after the tour
From a booking fee
From the city council
quests.correctAnswer: From voluntary payments after the tour
quests.hint: The word "free" and the phrase "tips only" work together here.
quests.explanation: The tour costs nothing up front, and guides depend on tips that visitors choose to give. Nothing mentions a fee, a ticket or council funding.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: If floodwater is expected, move valuables and important papers upstairs and switch off gas and electricity at the mains before water reaches your home. Do not walk or drive through moving water, since even shallow flow can knock a person over. Listen to the radio for updates and follow instructions from the emergency services. If you are told to evacuate, take medication, documents and a phone charger, and go to the reception centre in the sports hall. If you cannot leave, go to the highest floor and signal from a window.
quests.question: What should someone do if they cannot leave a flooded home?
options: Move valuables to the reception centre in the sports hall
Go to the highest floor and signal from a window
Wait in the kitchen and switch the electricity back on
Walk through shallow water to reach the nearest road
quests.correctAnswer: Go to the highest floor and signal from a window
quests.hint: Instructions for an unusual case are usually the last ones in a safety notice.
quests.explanation: The final sentence covers people who cannot evacuate: go upstairs and signal for help. Walking through water is specifically warned against.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: To return an item bought online, log in to your account and choose "Start a return" next to the order. Print the label, attach it to the parcel, and drop it at any post office within thirty days. Refunds are made to your original payment method once the item has been checked, which usually takes five working days. Shoes must be unworn, and clothing must still have its tags.
quests.question: What comes immediately before dropping off the parcel?
options: Logging out of the account
Receiving the refund
Attaching the printed label
Checking the item
quests.correctAnswer: Attaching the printed label
quests.hint: Put the actions in order and choose the one just before the drop-off.
quests.explanation: The sequence is start a return, print, attach, drop off. Refund and checking come afterwards, at the store's end.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: All students must wear goggles and closed shoes in the laboratory. Long hair should be tied back, and food or drink must be left outside. If a chemical touches your skin, rinse it under running water for at least ten minutes and tell your teacher at once. Never taste or smell anything unless you have been told that it is safe.
quests.question: What is the purpose of these rules?
options: To protect students from harm during experiments
To reduce the cost of laboratory equipment
To limit the number of students in each class
To teach students about chemistry and its history
quests.correctAnswer: To protect students from harm during experiments
quests.hint: Look at the kinds of things the rules forbid or require and ask what they have in common.
quests.explanation: Goggles, tied-back hair, rinsing chemicals and avoiding tasting all reduce risk. The rules assume students already study chemistry, so teaching it is not their aim.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear Ms. Clarke, I am sorry that your sofa did not arrive on the promised day. A supplier delay left us without the model you ordered, and we should have told you sooner. It is now in stock and can be delivered on Friday between eight and noon. As a gesture of apology, we will take fifteen percent off your bill and deliver at no charge. Yours sincerely, Andrew Patel, Customer Care
quests.question: What is the writer's main purpose?
options: To recommend a different sofa from another supplier
To ask for payment of the outstanding balance in full
To cancel the order and return the customer's money
To apologise and offer a new delivery with compensation
quests.correctAnswer: To apologise and offer a new delivery with compensation
quests.hint: A complaint reply often has three parts: sorry, reason, offer. Which part does the most work?
quests.explanation: The letter apologises, explains the delay and offers a discount and free delivery. The order stays active, and no payment or new product is requested.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Dear tenants, the annual boiler inspection will take place next week. An engineer will visit each flat between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. on Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday, and the visit should take about forty minutes. Please choose a day by replying to this email. If nobody is home, the engineer cannot enter unless you have left written permission with the caretaker.
quests.question: What is the first thing tenants are asked to do?
options: Call the engineer directly
Give the caretaker a key
Book a boiler repair
Reply with their preferred day
quests.correctAnswer: Reply with their preferred day
quests.hint: Find the sentence that begins with a polite request.
quests.explanation: "Please choose a day by replying" is the direct request. Written permission is only needed for tenants who will not be home.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Every winter, the Hillside food bank sees demand rise sharply, but the number of volunteers falls as people travel or fall ill. We are looking for two or three people who can spare a morning a week, sorting donations and helping families choose groceries. No experience is needed, and training is provided on your first day. If you can help, please speak to Mrs. Ong at the front desk.
quests.question: What is the writer trying to achieve?
options: To find more helpers for the food bank
To advertise a training course for new staff
To thank the current volunteers for their help
To collect more food donations for the winter
quests.correctAnswer: To find more helpers for the food bank
quests.hint: After the problem is described, watch for the sentence that asks for something.
quests.explanation: The problem is fewer volunteers in winter, and the request for "two or three people" is the goal. Training is only a reassurance for newcomers.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: You are warmly invited to celebrate Mr. Halvorsen's retirement after thirty-one years at Fairview High School. Join us in the staff room on Friday, 20 June, at 4 p.m. for tea, cake and a few short speeches. Please do not bring gifts; instead, a card will be circulating for messages, and contributions to the school library fund are welcome. RSVP to Jana by Monday.
quests.question: What are guests invited to do instead of bringing gifts?
options: Bring their own cake
Confirm their attendance by phone
Sign a card or give to the library fund
Give a short speech
quests.correctAnswer: Sign a card or give to the library fund
quests.hint: A phrase such as "instead" tells you what replaces the forbidden thing.
quests.explanation: After asking for no gifts, the invitation offers a card and library donations. Speeches and cake are part of the party, and RSVP is a separate request.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: To whom it may concern: I am writing about the noise from the building site on Kent Street, where work regularly begins at six in the morning. As I understand it, the council permits construction only after eight. Twice this month I have contacted the site manager without any reply. I would appreciate it if you could look into the matter and let me know what action will be taken. Yours faithfully, Tomasz Wrona
quests.question: What does the writer want the council to do?
options: Contact the site manager for him
Stop all building on Kent Street
Change the permitted hours to six
Investigate the early noise and respond
quests.correctAnswer: Investigate the early noise and respond
quests.hint: The polite request in the second half of a letter states the writer's real goal.
quests.explanation: "Look into the matter and let me know" means investigate and reply. He does not ask for the work to end, only for the rule to be enforced.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Safety notice: Brightway Kitchen has recalled its 1.5-litre glass kettles with serial numbers beginning HK4. The handle may loosen during use and cause spills of hot water. Customers should stop using the kettle immediately and return it to the place of purchase for a full refund; a receipt is not required. Other Brightway kettles are not affected.
quests.question: What is true for owners of the kettle in question?
options: They must repair the handle themselves
They must send the serial number by post
They can return it without a receipt
They can keep using it carefully
quests.correctAnswer: They can return it without a receipt
quests.hint: A recall notice includes an instruction, a condition and an exception. Test each option against them.
quests.explanation: A receipt "is not required," so it can be returned without one. Continuing to use it is exactly what the notice advises against.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Hello Mr. Baptiste, thank you for getting in touch about your broadband. We checked your line and found no fault, so the slow speeds you noticed in the evenings are probably caused by many households using the network at once. We can move you to our faster package, which is unaffected by busy periods. If you would like this, reply YES and we will arrange it within two days.
quests.question: Why does the company suggest a faster package?
options: It would avoid slowdowns at busy times
It costs less each month
The current line is faulty
The old package is being discontinued
quests.correctAnswer: It would avoid slowdowns at busy times
quests.hint: First find the cause of the customer's problem, then see how the offer answers it.
quests.explanation: The cause is heavy evening use, and the faster package is not affected by busy periods. The company says clearly that there is no fault.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: From today, all meeting rooms must be booked through the new online calendar rather than by email. Bookings made by email will no longer be recognised, and rooms left unoccupied for fifteen minutes will be released to other staff. The change is meant to stop rooms being reserved and then left empty. Guidance videos are available on the staff portal.
quests.question: What problem is the new system intended to solve?
options: Emails being too long for anyone to read
Meetings running late because of poor planning
Rooms being reserved but not used
Rooms being too small for the meetings held there
quests.correctAnswer: Rooms being reserved but not used
quests.hint: One sentence states the aim of the change directly.
quests.explanation: "Reserved and then left empty" is the problem. The fifteen-minute rule is the tool used to fix it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Our Year 9 students spent last Friday at the harbour, where a local marine biologist showed them how to test water quality. Pupils collected samples, measured temperature, and compared their results with data from ten years ago. The class will present their findings to the town council in March, and parents are welcome to attend the presentation.
quests.question: What is the main purpose of this item in the newsletter?
options: To announce a new science teacher for Year 9
To ask parents for money towards a new trip
To warn about polluted water in the harbour
To report on a class trip and an upcoming event
quests.correctAnswer: To report on a class trip and an upcoming event
quests.hint: Newsletter items usually tell what happened and what happens next.
quests.explanation: The first half reports the trip and the last sentence looks ahead to the presentation. Nothing suggests a request for money or a pollution warning.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: We are hiring a warehouse assistant for our busy distribution centre. Working days are Tuesday to Saturday, and the shift starts at 6 a.m. You will pick and pack orders, check deliveries, and keep your area tidy. We offer paid training, free parking, and a bonus for good attendance. Applicants must be at least eighteen and able to lift up to fifteen kilograms.
quests.question: What must every applicant be able to do?
options: Work on Sundays as well as weekdays
Lift up to fifteen kilograms
Drive a delivery van around the region
Train new members of staff on site
quests.correctAnswer: Lift up to fifteen kilograms
quests.hint: Ignore the benefits. Look for the sentence that lists requirements.
quests.explanation: The requirements are age and lifting ability. Paid training is a benefit the company gives, not a skill applicants need.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Gas pipe replacement on Ridge Avenue will begin on 6 October and last about eight weeks. Work will happen between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., and one lane will remain open, controlled by temporary traffic lights. Delays of up to twenty minutes are expected at busy times, so drivers should consider using Bridge Road. Access to homes and shops will be maintained throughout.
quests.question: Why does the notice suggest Bridge Road?
options: Ridge Avenue will be slow at busy times
The shops have moved
Ridge Avenue will be closed completely
Bridge Road has no traffic lights
quests.correctAnswer: Ridge Avenue will be slow at busy times
quests.hint: The suggestion comes right after a warning. What is the warning about?
quests.explanation: Delays of up to twenty minutes explain the alternative route. One lane stays open, so the road is not fully closed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Hi Dario, are you free to swap shifts on Saturday? My sister's wedding is that afternoon and I've promised to be there by two. I could cover your Sunday morning in exchange, and I'll also take your next closing shift if that helps. Let me know by tonight so I can tell Mrs. Bell before she finalises the rota. Thanks a lot, Ines
quests.question: What is Ines asking Dario to do?
options: Work her Saturday shift in return for her Sunday help
Attend the wedding in her place on Saturday
Talk to Mrs. Bell about the rota on her behalf
Work every closing shift for the next month
quests.correctAnswer: Work her Saturday shift in return for her Sunday help
quests.hint: Work out who takes which day before you choose.
quests.explanation: She wants him to take Saturday, and she offers to cover his Sunday morning. Mrs. Bell is only the person who must be told.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Next Thursday's assembly will be led by the student council, and we need your ideas! Should the school have longer lunch breaks, a recycling scheme, or a later start on Mondays? Put your suggestion in the blue box outside the office by Tuesday, and we will read the most popular ones aloud. Please be positive: ideas about improving things are more useful than complaints.
quests.question: What kind of suggestions does the council want?
options: Ideas for songs to be sung in assemblies
Votes for the new members of the council
Constructive ideas for improving the school
Complaints about certain teachers and their lessons
quests.correctAnswer: Constructive ideas for improving the school
quests.hint: The last sentence explains which kind of message is welcome and which is not.
quests.explanation: The council asks for improvements rather than complaints. The examples given, such as recycling, show the type of idea they mean.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear customer, from 1 April our standard electricity rate will rise from 24 to 27 cents per unit because of higher wholesale costs. Customers who pay by direct debit will receive a three-percent discount, and those with a fixed-rate plan will not be affected until their contract ends. You do not need to do anything, but if you would like to compare plans, visit the page below.
quests.question: What is the main reason for this letter?
options: To advertise a discount for new customers
To inform customers about a price increase
To ask customers to pay early
To announce a company merger
quests.correctAnswer: To inform customers about a price increase
quests.hint: Ask what the customer needs to know, even though no action is required.
quests.explanation: The rate is going up, and the rest of the letter explains who is affected. The discount applies to existing customers who pay by direct debit.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: From next Monday, the 6 p.m. spin class moves to 6:45 to make room for a new beginners' class. Members already booked on the old time will be contacted individually, and anyone who cannot attend the later session may cancel without penalty until Sunday noon. The 6 a.m. and lunchtime classes are unchanged. We apologise for the inconvenience and hope the new schedule suits more members.
quests.question: Who will be contacted individually?
options: Beginners joining the new class
All members of the gym
The instructors
Members booked on the old class time
quests.correctAnswer: Members booked on the old class time
quests.hint: The sentence with "already booked" describes a specific group.
quests.explanation: Only those with the 6 p.m. booking are affected and will be contacted. Beginners are simply the reason the schedule is changing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Please enjoy the exhibition at your own pace. The rooms are arranged in chronological order, beginning with the earliest tools on the ground floor and ending with modern instruments upstairs. Touch screens beside each display give more detail, and audio guides can be borrowed at the entrance. Photography without flash is welcome. The cafe on the first floor closes thirty minutes before the museum.
quests.question: How are the exhibition rooms organised?
options: By country of origin
From the oldest objects to the newest
By the size of the objects
From the cheapest to the most valuable
quests.correctAnswer: From the oldest objects to the newest
quests.hint: One unfamiliar word in the second sentence answers this. Use the rest of the sentence to decode it.
quests.explanation: "Earliest tools" at the start and "modern instruments" at the end show the order is by age. You can understand "chronological" from the context.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear Mr. Delgado, thank you for staying with us last week. Your opinion helps us improve, so we would be grateful if you could spend two minutes answering a short survey about your stay. Those who complete it before the end of the month will be entered into a draw to win a weekend break. You can find the survey at the link below. Kind regards, Guest Relations
quests.question: Why does the email mention the weekend break?
options: To thank guests for staying at the hotel
To encourage guests to complete the survey
To advertise the hotel's rooms for the summer
To make up for a bad experience during a stay
quests.correctAnswer: To encourage guests to complete the survey
quests.hint: Notice where the prize appears: it comes attached to a condition.
quests.explanation: The prize is offered only to those who complete the survey, so it works as an incentive. There is no sign that the stay went badly.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Resident parking permits expire on 30 September. To renew, log in to the council website, confirm your address and vehicle details, and pay the annual fee of forty dollars. New permits will be posted within ten days, but there is no gap in cover if you renew before the expiry date. Drivers who forget to renew may be fined.
quests.question: What happens if you renew before 30 September?
options: You pay a reduced fee
You receive the permit at once
You skip confirming your address
You stay covered without a break
quests.correctAnswer: You stay covered without a break
quests.hint: Turn the phrase "no gap in cover" into everyday words.
quests.explanation: Renewing early means continuous cover, even though the permit arrives later by post. The passage mentions no discount.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Subject: New expense system. Dear colleagues, from 1 November we will stop using paper claim forms. Instead, you will photograph your receipts and upload them through the finance app, and payments will arrive in your account within five working days rather than the current three weeks. Paper forms received after 31 October will not be processed. A short training session will be held on Monday at 10 a.m. in Room 4. Please attend if you claim expenses regularly. Regards, Lena Fischer, Finance
quests.question: What is one advantage of the new system for employees?
options: They can skip the training
They can claim larger amounts
They no longer need receipts
They are repaid more quickly
quests.correctAnswer: They are repaid more quickly
quests.hint: Look for a comparison between the new and old ways.
quests.explanation: Five working days replaces three weeks, so repayment is faster. Receipts are still needed because they are photographed and uploaded.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear Mrs. Adeyemi, your appointment with Dr. Kaur at the eye clinic has been rescheduled to Wednesday, 9 July, at 11:20 a.m. Please arrive fifteen minutes early to complete a registration form. As drops will be used to widen your pupils, your vision may be blurred afterwards, so you should not drive and may wish to bring someone with you. If this date is inconvenient, telephone 555-0147 before 4 p.m. on Friday.
quests.question: Why is Mrs. Adeyemi advised not to drive?
options: Her eyesight may be affected after the examination
The clinic has no parking for patients who drive
The clinic is a long way from her home
The appointment is very early in the morning
quests.correctAnswer: Her eyesight may be affected after the examination
quests.hint: The advice contains a "so" and the cause comes just before it.
quests.explanation: The eye drops may blur her vision, and the advice not to drive follows from that. Parking and distance are not mentioned.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Attention, please. The library will close in fifteen minutes. Anyone borrowing books should bring them to the front desk now, as the self-service machines will be switched off in ten minutes. Please save your work and log off any computers. The library reopens tomorrow at nine o'clock, and tonight's returns can be left in the box outside.
quests.question: Why should borrowers go to the desk now?
options: The self-service machines will soon stop working
The computers are about to break down for the night
The library will not reopen at nine o'clock tomorrow
Returns must be handed in personally at the desk
quests.correctAnswer: The self-service machines will soon stop working
quests.hint: A short word can link an instruction to its reason. Find it in the second sentence.
quests.explanation: The machines will be switched off in ten minutes, which is earlier than closing time, so borrowers must go to the desk. Returns have their own separate box.
